subject: Urgent: p99 surge — hosted model latency, KV cache invalidation suspected

Date: Fri, 24 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: sudden p99/p95 latency spike on production — please help

Hi Karthik,

We saw a sharp jump in user-facing latencies starting ~08:45 PDT this morning for our hosted inference calls (model: gptx-13b-redwood-v1). p95 climbed from ~120ms to ~650ms and p99 was hitting ~2.1s — our error budget alarms also tripped briefly. Impacting real-time search completions for our storefront.

Sample request IDs: req-7a2f4, req-7a2f7, req-7a32b. We noticed a corresponding increase in 504s and a spike in per-request CPU on the hosted cluster. No config changes on our side. Can you triage? This is causing checkout slowdowns.

Happy to provide logs or give you access to a short call.

—Sara

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 24 Apr 2027 10:04:22 -0700
Subject: Re: sudden p99/p95 latency spike on production — please help

Quick summary of what the infra team sees (preliminary):
- Timeline: config rollout to region us-west2 at 08:40 PDT changed a TTL policy used by the hosted KV/prefix cache (cache-control: global-ttl reduced from 6h->5m in the rollout).
- Symptom: massive cold misses as the long-lived prefixes were evicted; KV cache miss rate jumped from ~3% to ~78% for traffic at 08:45 — this aligns with the latency spike window.
- Impact (observed): p95 -> 120ms to ~650ms, p99 -> ~220ms to ~2100ms for affected model variants. Error rate (504/timeout) rose from 0.03% to 0.8% for the short window.

Attachments: we pushed a small bundle with host logs and the eviction time-series (hosted-p99-spike-20270424-logs.zip). The kv-eviction-heap-graph shows the sudden TTL cascade at 08:40. Correlation queries in correlation-query.txt.

Short-term mitigation options we've applied or can apply immediately:
- Roll back the TTL change in us-west2 (we can rollback the global cache-policy in 10m).
- Enable cache-warmup job for hot prefixes (will start filling within ~2–5 minutes, but p99 will take longer to normalize).
- Route BrightRetail traffic temporarily to a warm Dedicated pool or to us-east1 where TTL remains intact (need permission to failover).

We are leaning towards rollback + targeted cache-warmup as the fastest path. If we need zero-risk, route to dedicated pool while we stabilize.

I will continue with a full RCA and a mitigation plan to prevent global TTL rollouts without staged canaries.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
SRE, Serving Runtime — Redwood Inference
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Jensen <sara.jensen@bright-retail.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 24 Apr 2027 10:12:45 -0700
Subject: Re: sudden p99/p95 latency spike on production — please help

Hi Sara — sorry for the disruption. We're actively mitigating. Rishi has identified the likely cause as a TTL reduction in the global cache policy that resulted in large-scale prefix evictions.

Immediate plan:
1) We'll roll back the TTL change in us-west2 now (ETA ~10m).
2) Run a targeted cache-warmup for your top ~2k prefixes — should bring p95 close to baseline in ~3–6 minutes and p99 within ~15–30 minutes.
3) If you prefer, we can failover your traffic to a dedicated warm pool for a short window while we stabilize — we need an approval to change routing.

Can you confirm if you'd like us to failover, or is rollback + warmup ok? We will keep you updated every 15 minutes until fully normalized.

Best,
Monica Patel
Customer Success Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: urgent: p99 surge — hosted model latency, KV cache invalidation suspected

Folks — quick executive note and summary for records / commercial follow-up:
- Incident summary: 2027-04-24 08:40 PDT — config rollout reduced global cache TTL in us-west2 causing large-scale KV/prefix evictions and a transient p99/p95 regression affecting BrightRetail and a small handful of other customers. Root cause: insufficient rollout canary for cache-policy change.
- Customer impact: BrightRetail saw p95 jump to ~650ms and p99 to ~2.1s for ~20 minutes; some timeouts and retail checkout slowdowns were reported.
- Actions taken: rollback in region, targeted warmup, and one-hour follow-up health checks.
- Next steps: engineering to provide RCA doc and updated rollout guard (Rishi). Proposal for commercial remediation: 10% hosting credit for the affected hourly window + post mortem call with BrightRetail (Monica/Karthik to own).

Marissa/Laura — please advise on the credit approval path; we should also consider a short note to other customers potentially impacted.

Thanks — Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
